findings.summary: The Factory Method trade-off bullet puts the problem and an alternative in one line, and it brings in 'static factory' without defining it. This is easy to confuse with Factory Method.
findings.evidence: "A subclass per product explodes the class count; use a static factory if no extension is needed"
findings.fix: Split it into a downside bullet and an alternative bullet, and define the term: "static factory = a plain static method that returns the object".

findings.summary: The Prototype definition sits under 'Copy and Build Bugs' before any bug is stated, and that bullet mixes a concept into a mistakes section.
findings.evidence: "Prototype pays off when an object is costly to create but cheap to copy"
findings.fix: Drop this bullet, since pages 1 and 4 already cover it, or move it to the Remember section.

findings.summary: Must-Know bullets pack two or more ideas into one line.
findings.evidence: "Thread-safe: enum or eager init; inject, don't go global" and "Abstract Factory: one interface, a product family; easy to add families, hard to add products"
findings.fix: Split each into separate one-idea bullets: thread-safe options, then the advice to inject rather than use a global. For Abstract Factory, give the structure and the extension trade-off their own bullets.

findings.summary: The 'Shallow vs deep' pitfall is a bare label followed by a callout, so it is not parallel to the other pitfalls and does not name a failure.
findings.evidence: "Shallow vs deep" / "Mutating a shallow clone changes the original; deep-copy mutable fields."
findings.fix: Rewrite it as a pitfall bullet like the others: "Shallow clone with mutable fields: editing the clone changes the original".
